I have farmed this land for 40 years. I went to primary school, so I can read fertilizer bags and do my accounts, but I learned farming by doing it and watching others. Last year my wheat got 520 kg per mu and my maize got 580 kg per mu. This year I will manage them almost the same way, because change is risky and last year was decent.

I have 20.4 mu total. I put 18 mu in wheat-maize rotation, and I keep 2.4 mu on the south edge for millet.

The wheat went in last October. For base fertilizer I put one 50 kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu and half a bag of urea. Now it is spring and the wheat looks a bit yellow after winter. At green-up I will spread 40 jin — that is 20 kg — of urea per mu. When it joints I will put another 20 jin per mu. Total nitrogen for the wheat is about 30 kg per mu. I get about 10 kg phosphorus and 8 kg potassium per mu from the compound fertilizer. I will irrigate three times: green-up water, jointing water, and heading water. I already sprayed herbicide once in early spring. Before grain filling I will spray fungicide once more. I rotary till before planting wheat every year. I expect 530 kg per mu if the weather is normal.

For summer maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in early June. I use hybrid seed — I will buy the same kind my neighbor Lao Zhang used last year, his got 590 kg per mu. At planting I put one 50 kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu. When the maize reaches big trumpet stage, I side-dress with 60 jin — 30 kg — of urea per mu. That gives about 22 kg nitrogen per mu total, plus 8 kg phosphorus and 6 kg potassium. I irrigate twice: once at planting if it is dry, and once at tasseling. I spray herbicide at planting, and one insecticide spray if I see corn borers. I do no-tillage direct seeding — there is no time to plough between wheat harvest and maize planting. I hire the seeding machine for 50 yuan per mu. I expect 590 kg per mu.

For the 2.4 mu of millet, I rotary till in mid-May and sow the local improved variety. I put half a bag — 25 kg — of compound fertilizer per mu, and topdress with 20 jin of urea when it starts growing. That is about 10 kg nitrogen, 4 kg phosphorus, and 3 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice and spray once for weeds. Expected yield is 280 kg per mu. The millet is partly for family eating.

Now about money. Urea is 2.6 yuan per jin this year, up from last year. Compound fertilizer is 3.2 yuan per jin. For the whole farm I will spend about 14,000 yuan on fertilizer. My sons work in Handan city and send money home, so I can manage it. But I still count every yuan. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than risk losing yield. A bad harvest is a disaster — I cannot feed seven people or sell grain for cash. Wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. I do not cut back on fertilizer to buy more pesticide. The bugs are not bad every year, but the crops always need food.
